subject: Aurelia Health — PO template, consolidated invoice cadence, and pricing guardrails
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurelia PO template + invoice cadence question

Hi Tessa / Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Aurelia is excited about the performance numbers. Procurement looped me in with a couple of operational questions before we finalize the SOW:

- We operate on blanket POs and need the vendor to accept PO numbers on all invoices. Attached is our standard PO template (Aurelia_PO_template.pdf). Can Redwood accept a blanket PO referencing a 12-month engagement?
- Invoice cadence: our AP runs biweekly but prefers consolidated monthly invoices for services. Would Redwood be able to issue a single consolidated invoice each month that includes line-level usage detail and the PO number?
- Net terms: Aurelia’s standard is Net 30. Separately, they occasionally ask for an early-payment discount (1% if paid within 10 days). Is that something you can provide?
- Price protection: procurement prefers a 12-month price lock for committed baseline usage. We understand usage may vary — can we get a guaranteed price for the baseline?

Please confirm what options are feasible and any implementation steps (e.g., invoices format, remittance contact). We’d like to avoid manual splits or multiple invoices per month if possible.

Ellen
Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health Systems

Attachment: Aurelia_PO_template.pdf (application/pdf, 112KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia PO template + invoice cadence question

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. High level: we can accept a blanket PO and include the PO number on invoices; we can also provide a consolidated monthly invoice with line-level detail. A few things to note from finance/legal:

- PO acceptance: Redwood can accept the blanket PO as the commercial order. We’ll ask legal to confirm the signature flow, but operationally we can anchor invoices to the PO number you provide.
- Consolidated monthly invoice: yes — single invoice/month with subscription lines + usage lines and per-line breakdown is our standard for enterprise onboarding. We can also provide a CSV export for your AP system.
- Net terms & early payment: Net 30 is our default. We do not typically run a 1% early-pay program for usage invoices. Two alternatives we can offer: 1) a 2% annual prepay credit applied if Aurelia prepays an annual committed amount, or 2) a limited early-pay credit of 0.5% on invoices under $50k.
- Price protection: we can lock prices for the committed baseline for 12 months provided the baseline is defined in the SOW (committed monthly compute/requests). Overages would be billed at a usage rate as discussed in the quote.

Connor and Ben — can you review the invoice split example and confirm billing contact details and whether finance needs any specific fields from our side? I’ve attached the PO for reference.

Thanks,
Tessa
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Aurelia_PO_template.pdf (application/pdf, 112KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia PO template + invoice cadence question

Ellen — quick operational note and a sample. Attached is a proposed invoice sample (proposed_invoice_sample.xlsx) that shows how we would present: (A) recurring subscription fees, (B) variable usage by product, and (C) a month-to-date summary.

Proposed approach we recommend:
- One consolidated invoice per calendar month (issued on the 1st business day), with the PO number in the invoice header.
- Line-level detail for every SKU / model family and token band; we also include total tokens and effective unit price per line for clarity.
- Remittance & allocation: please provide the AP remit-to contact and any internal fund codes. Our AR team can include up to two internal references on each invoice (PO + cost center code).
- Terms compromise: Redwood prefers consistent terms across invoice types; if Aurelia needs early-pay incentives, the cleanest approach is the 2% annual prepay credit Tessa mentioned (applies to the committed baseline only). Operationally simpler than mixing multiple net terms.

Related links: HS-987654 (your HubSpot record).

Attachment: proposed_invoice_sample.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 24KB)

—Connor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia PO template + invoice cadence question

Tessa — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from procurement after reviewing Connor’s sample: 

1) Consolidated monthly invoice with PO number sounds good. Please confirm the invoice will be in PDF with an attached CSV for import.
2) Price lock: procurement needs explicit language in the SOW that baseline pricing will not increase for 12 months except for mutually agreed change orders. Can you have legal draft that clause?
3) Early-payment: the business is pushing for a 1% if paid in 10 days — they’re willing to limit to invoices under $100k. Is Redwood able to accept that condition for this account?
4) Acceptance of blanket PO as order: procurement would like written confirmation that Redwood will accept the blanket PO (PO number will be provided by next week) and that invoices referencing that PO meet their acceptance criteria for automated matching.

If we can get written confirmation on (1)–(4) and a billing contact (name + email + remit address), procurement will route the PO and we can get the SOW signed.

Thanks,
Ellen

On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 at 11:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list...
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia PO template + invoice cadence question

Ellen — thanks, and great list. To be explicit and put the options in writing so procurement can proceed: 

1) Invoice format & cadence
- Redwood will issue a single consolidated invoice per calendar month (invoice date: 1st business day). Invoice will be PDF. We will attach a machine-readable CSV/line-item export suitable for AP import.

2) PO acceptance
- Redwood will accept Aurelia’s blanket PO as the commercial order. We will include the PO number in the invoice header and in the invoice metadata so it can be matched by your AP system. This satisfies our acceptance criteria for standard POs.

3) Net terms & early-pay option
- Standard: Net 30 across invoices.
- Early-pay: Redwood cannot commit to a blanket 1% early-pay discount for usage invoices. As a commercially viable alternative we can offer either:
  a) 2% credit for annual prepayment against the committed baseline (applies only to prepaid committed value), or
  b) 0.5% early-pay credit on invoices under $75k if Aurelia elects early payment within 10 days.
Please indicate which option procurement prefers; we can encode the selection in the SOW.

4) Price protection
- Redwood will include a 12-month price protection clause for the defined committed baseline if the baseline is included in the SOW and invoiceable committed amount is prepaid or committed in the contract. Overages billed above baseline will be at the quoted usage rates. Redwood legal will provide the specific clause for inclusion.

Operational next steps:
- Please share AP remit contact (name, email, remit address) and cost-center/payment references.
- If Aurelia is comfortable with option (a) or (b) above, we will circulate a short commercial addendum and DocuSign link for signatures.
- I’ve attached our billing onboarding checklist to make the handoff to AR smooth.

Ben — can you follow up with finance on whether the 0.5% early-pay for < $75k invoices is feasible and any limits on credits?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: billing_onboarding_checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 18KB)
